page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory. The underlying hardware features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.2 GHz. This configuration provides 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing a dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the e2-highmem-2 resides in lower performance tiers for compute and memory throughput. The single-core stress-ng performance is measured at 1101.98, while the multi-core score is 1451.88, both falling into the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached transfers reaching 80.53 GB/sec and uncached large block transfers dropping to 12.0 GB/sec read and 10.51 GB/sec write. Geekbench evaluations reflect similar trends, yielding a single-core score of 841.0 and a multi-core score of 1028.0.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core alongside modest processing capabilities, the instance represents a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU performance. It is suitable for small-scale database operations, lightweight caching layers, text processing, and basic web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over raw computational throughput.
